parsed.explanation: Federal/provincial protections for gender identity/expression, hate-crime listing, identity-based prison placement and documented recourse operate in a functioning rule-of-law state, with no documented traveller-facing criminalisation, border, facility or custody restriction. Offset by rising police-reported hate crime, high verbal-abuse prevalence in a broad LGBT survey, an organised anti-trans movement, and subnational school/health rollbacks shielded by override clauses. Visitor exposure is mainly harassment and uneven provincial practice, not detention or state targeting.

entry_documents.protection: National documents offer an X marker; most provinces offer self-declaration recognition. No trans-specific border friction documented. Resident-facing recognition is climate signal only.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between visitor documents and border screening; silence in well-documented state is moderately positive.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2022 report alleged pattern of abuse/sexual assault of gender-diverse prisoners; litigation over treatment/placement. Detention of a visitor for being trans not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National rule: placement by gender identity; head of government committed review; officers mindful of safety in 2022 study.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a visitor were detained for an unrelated offence, identity-based placement mitigates but documented custodial abuse remains a risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward or public-accommodation ban documented. Provincial divergence documented mainly for schools/documents.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Federal and provincial human-rights protections cover gender identity/expression; one province publishes policy/case law route to recourse.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Provincial protections interact with federal protection from 2017; no federal facility exposure documented.

care_services.exposure: One province's 2024 health/education/sport statutes shielded by 2025 override; content and visitor effect not documented.
care_services.protection: No documented denial of emergency or routine care to visitors; surgery-consideration rule is resident custody-related and not counted as visitor care.
care_services.interaction: Uncertain whether shielded health statutes affect travelling minors or care access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Rising organised anti-trans movement and two provinces' school-pronoun/healthcare rollbacks signal hostile framing in parts of country.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2017 federal hate-motivation provisions and human-rights act explicitly list gender identity/expression; upper chamber 67-11.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Override clauses limit judicial recourse for resident school/health rules, but no visitor-facing threat-framing law documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: One province requires parental consent before under-16 student uses preferred name/gender identity, enacted with override; legal challenge followed.
minors_guardians.protection: Travelling parent/guardian can provide that consent; comparable anti-bullying laws exist in many provinces.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor enrolled locally faces consent/exposure in that province; shielded statutes in another province have undocumented minor effect.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police-reported hate crimes rose six years, +169% since 2018; 2022 survey: 39% of 2SLGBTQI+ respondents (broad, not trans-specific) reported identity violence in 5 years, mostly verbal, 17% physical.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime listing provides enforcement stream; national hate-crime volume 4,882 in 2024, not disaggregated by gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Harassment exposure is real but no documented police targeting of visitors or impunity pattern for trans victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2012 submission gaps predate 2017 protections and are not current exposure; other provinces' document procedures and border rules not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented provincial human-rights commission route with published policy/case law; federal protection provides additional recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are stronger where provincial code is documented; override-shielded laws reduce recourse for resident school/health issues.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar strong equality law, X/self-declaration documents and oversight, but this case has documented rising hate crime, organised anti-trans movement and override-shielded provincial rollbacks, placing it lower than 0.85.
Closest: protections operate and harassment/assault risk is moderate with recourse dependent on reporting. This dossier matches that profile, with extra provincial divergence for minors.
Higher than 0.65 because no documented care refusal, prolonged detention or intrusive questioning of visitors; remedies and protections are broader, though street harassment remains.
Well above 0.55: no universal ward/facility exclusion by document marker, no systematic denial of treatment, and identity-based custody placement is protective rather than birth-sex based.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: federal protections and identity-based placement protect visitors in principle, while provincial variation—especially under-16 parental-consent schooling and override-shielded health/education statutes—creates uneven exposure for travelling families. No documented border, facility or criminal exposure for adult visitors. Main operative risk if outed is social hostility/harassment in a rising hate-crime climate, with functioning recourse in at least documented provinces. That combination sits in Reduced Risk, below strong 0.85 cases due to documented hostility and subnational rollbacks.
